A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPM/GPO research despite the changed title and terminology. All 34 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cyclic-preference, RewardBench, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench and six-task downstream evaluations, including architecture ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original cyclic-preference, RewardBench, AlpacaEval and MT-Bench results, architecture ablations and a new LN-GPO evaluation in Appendix E.

M1.justification: v2 adds length-normalized GPO in Remark E.1, dividing the policy log-ratio by response length. The original GPM architecture, scale gate, embedding normalization and GPO objective remain unchanged; moving implementation material from Appendix A.2 into Section 4.2 is not a new component.

E1.justification: The principal training datasets and preference/alignment benchmarks remain. However, v2 removes v1's explicit six-task LM-Harness/Leaderboard evaluations while Section 6.3 still states that GSM8K, MMLU and other tasks were evaluated. This leaves uncertainty about reduced actual coverage versus reduced reporting. Appendix F supplies illustrative UltraFeedback cases rather than an established new evaluation population.

E2.justification: The tables retain BT reward models, the cyclic random-guess reference and SPPO/GPO comparisons. PairRM and SimPO are not newly evaluated baselines. However, v2 Section 6.3 describes both GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4-turbo responses as comparison references, whereas the tables identify them as evaluators. Whether the AlpacaEval reference comparator changed is therefore ambiguous.

E3.justification: v2 reports decontaminated Skywork training data, changes the Gemma-2B learning rate from 1e-5 to 2e-6, and adds a Gemma-2-9B configuration. It removes the DeepSeek-V2 evaluator and the documented six-task evaluation protocols, while adding GPT-4o-mini length-controlled win rates and an LN-GPO experiment. These are substantial reported setting changes, not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds a limited length-normalization experiment in Table 7 and two UltraFeedback case studies discussing possible cycles under fixed criteria in Appendix F. The embedding-dimension, scale-gate and L2-normalization ablation designs remain, although their numerical outcomes change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run aggregation, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The revised tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: RewardBench Gemma-2B BT/best-GPM averages change from 68.9/74.5, with dimension 8 best, to 74.85/82.29, with dimension 6 best, under revised training settings. AlpacaEval, MT-Bench and architecture-ablation scores are extensively replaced. Gemma-2-9B and LN-GPO results are added; DeepSeek-V2 and six-task suite results are removed. The matched cyclic-preference scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 5.1 and Appendix C.4, claiming an O(1/sqrt(T)) GPO convergence bound under realizability and bounded preference scores, with a multiplicative-weights argument. Appendix B also replaces the probability-based von Neumann winner condition with an expected-score condition. The spectral representation theorem previously numbered A.3 is retained as Theorem 4.5.

C1.justification: The efficient, expressive GPM and preference-score-based GPO contributions remain. v2 removes the abstract's specific 5.6% and 9.3% improvement claims and narrows the introduction's downstream conclusion to possible improvement. Its conclusion also drops v1's claim of outperforming supervised pair-preference models.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the interpretation that larger embeddings generally improve performance with model- and task-dependent optimal dimensions. It adds reasoning about fixed-criterion preference cycles, but removes v1's explicit overfitting/generalization limitation, the explanation of weaker scale-gate effects in larger models, and the caution about applying length-control calibration to other evaluators.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that cyclic accuracy uses training-dataset responses with different comparison pairs; this is additional disclosure, not an established split change. It revises the Gemma-2B learning-rate documentation and adds a Gemma-2-9B training setting. Frameworks, hardware and code-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Freund and Schapire's multiplicative-weights work and Meng et al.'s SimPO, while removing references to LiPO, DeepSeek-V2 and the Open LLM Leaderboard. The central positioning against scalar reward models and pairwise preference models remains; much of the related-work discussion is simply moved to Appendix D.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it changes the title and representation terminology, shortens the abstract, moves preference-RL background into Section 3.3, promotes implementation material into Section 4.2, reverses the RewardBench/cyclic subsection order, and restructures the appendices into separate optimization, proof, related-work, experiment and example sections.

P2.justification: The three figures are retained with relabeling, resizing and relocation. Table presentation changes substantially: GPT-4o-mini and MT-Bench results move to the appendix, five result tables disappear, an LN-GPO table is added, and the GPT-4o-mini table gains length-controlled columns. Captions, highlighting and table placement are also revised.

improvement.justification: v2 improves access to implementation details, narrows some overstated claims and adds LN-GPO. However, it removes explicit limitations and result tables for tasks still invoked in Section 6.3. Its new convergence proof in Appendix C.4 does not justify dropping the nonvanishing rho/2 terms before concluding a vanishing gap. Appendix E.1 also retains a claim of consistent L2 benefits contradicted by revised Table 4. These issues reduce rigor and evidential clarity despite the useful additions.
